questions.q: Put in order of sustainability: recycle, reduce, reuse.
questions.model: Which uses no new resources at all? Reduce. Which uses the item again without processing? Reuse. Which still needs energy to process? Recycle. So: reduce, reuse, recycle.

questions.q: How much energy does recycling aluminium save (approximately)?
questions.a: About 95% of the energy of making new aluminium.
Energy and transport for collecting and sorting.

questions.q: Core: Sort your household recycling for one day into metal, glass, paper and plastic. Record what you find and how each is recycled.
questions.a: Pupils' own; metal melted and recast, glass crushed and melted, paper pulped, plastic sorted, shredded and melted.
questions.model: Teacher shows one item: a steel tin: sorted by magnet, melted and made into new steel.

questions.q: Extend: Evaluate recycling glass bottles against reusing them (portal response box).
questions.a: Reuse saves more energy (just washing); recycling needs melting at high temperature; but reuse needs collection systems.

questions.q: Stretch: Why can paper only be recycled a limited number of times?
questions.a: The cellulose fibres get shorter each time until they are too weak.

questions.q: The most sustainable choice is usually...
Big question: is recycling always the best thing to do with waste?
questions.a: No: reducing and reusing are better; recycling still uses energy, but it is better than landfill.
